title: High-rate continuous-variable quantum key distribution coexisting with Tb/s coherent classical transmission in hollow-core fiber
authors: Xitao Ji, Siyu Chen, Peng Li, Mingming Zhang, Yilun Chen, Jun Gao, Rui Lin, Bacco Davide, Siqi Yan, Ming Tang
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) can provide secret keys with security rooted in quantum mechanics, but operation alongside high-capacity classical traffic remains limited by the excess-noise budget of weak quantum states in conventional solid-core fiber. Here, we combine ultralow-loss anti-resonant hollow-core fiber with residual-carrier-assisted discrete-modulation continuous-variable QKD (DM-CV-QKD) to address both propagation-induced coexistence noise and low-SNR phase recovery. Over a 24.3-km hollow-core link with 3.3-dB end-to-end loss, a dual-polarization 15-Gbaud DM-CV-QKD channel achieves an average asymptotic secret-key rate (SKR) of 153.22 Mb/s and a finite-size SKR of 149.99 Mb/s, while 39 coherent wavelength-division-multiplexed channels deliver an aggregate data rate of 7.6 Tb/s and a net data rate of 7.2 Tb/s. The system can even sustain a positive SKR under a high classical launch power of up to 15 dBm, without an optical bandpass filter (BPF). Finite-size analysis against collective attacks further yields a projected positive secret-key rate at a 100-km-equivalent condition. These results show that an anti-resonant hollow-core fiber, combined with carrier-assisted phase recovery, can greatly extend the operating regime of shared-fiber quantum-secured coherent links, pointing to a promising approach for integrating high-rate CV-QKD with high-capacity optical networks.
summary: The paper presents an experimental demonstration showing how to integrate high-rate continuous-variable QKD with Tb/s classical communication in a shared optical link. By utilizing anti-resonant hollow-core fiber, the system effectively suppresses noise accumulation that typically limits quantum transmission. This approach establishes a promising pathway for realizing secure, high-capacity quantum internet infrastructure.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is enabling high-rate continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) to operate reliably alongside massive classical optical data streams within a shared fiber infrastructure.
main_result: The authors demonstrated that using an anti-resonant hollow-core fiber combined with residual-carrier assistance allows for achieving simultaneous rates of 153.22 Mb/s quantum key rate and 7.2 Tb/s classical data rate over 24.3 km.
method: The system employs dual-polarization, high-baudrate modulation (15 Gbaud for QKD) and utilizes advanced digital signal processing (DSP) techniques at the receiver end for phase recovery and equalization.
model_or_system: The physical platform is an anti-resonant hollow-core fiber (AR-HCF), which confines light primarily in air to minimize nonlinear interactions with silica glass. The quantum channel uses CV-QKD, while the classical channel supports multiple wavelength-division multiplexed channels.
key_observables: Secret Key Rate (SKR) ($	ext{Mb/s}$), aggregate data rate ($	ext{Tb/s}$), and sustained positive SKR under high classical launch power.
important_parameters: 24.3 km link length, 15 Gbaud modulation, up to $15 	ext{ dBm}$ classical launch power, and projected extension to a $100	ext{-km-equivalent}$ condition.
main_assumptions: The performance relies on the physical advantage of air-core propagation to suppress noise sources like Four-Wave Mixing (FWM) and Spontaneous Raman Scattering (SpRS).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the AR-HCF structure and low attenuation, compare nonlinear noise spectra between SMF and HCFs, and show simulated SKR vs. distance curves demonstrating superior performance in HCF.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the coexistence challenge, then detailing the physical solution (AR-HCF) to mitigate noise, followed by implementing advanced signal processing techniques (DSP/equalization) for robust quantum reception, and finally quantifying the high achievable rates.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes the boundaries of practical quantum networking by solving the critical engineering problem of integrating weak quantum signals with powerful classical channels over long distances using novel fiber platforms.
